summary: The design addresses real gaps, but its highest risks are lifecycle integration, runner identification, and evidence ownership. The existing supervisor is merge/feature-only, the engine creates retries from the feature branch, and several pytest-specific helpers would silently mis-handle non-Python runners unless runner identity becomes explicit throughout.

suggestions.title: Make verdict execution a first-class supervisor receipt
suggestions.rationale: ValidationSupervisor.start currently accepts only merge/feature tiers and returns a BackgroundRegistration before completion; terminal status exposes outcome, exit code, and log references, not a structured verdict. report.append_suite writes temporary records without an EvidenceRef, while ExecutionEvidenceStore already provides content-addressed artifacts. Add one supervisor-owned run-and-verdict path used by both the seat tool and engine gate, persisting the verdict artifact before returning it.

suggestions.title: Validate the immutable attempt tree before acquiring the merge lock
suggestions.rationale: _consolidate mutates the attempt through extraction and lint, then performs fidelity and banned-import checks before the merge lock. SubWorktreeManager.create always forks from the feature branch, and _write_attempt_scope records that moving branch name as base_ref. The gate must run against the attempt worktree after all engine mutations and before merge, using the exact fork SHA; otherwise concurrent sibling merges can make selection cover the wrong tree.

suggestions.title: Match normalized command chains, not only argv[0]
suggestions.rationale: The UI test entry point is pnpm, while the proposed command is pnpm exec vitest; current pytest normalization only understands environment prefixes, uv run, and python -m pytest. A registry keyed solely by argv[0] would classify pnpm as unknown and cannot distinguish pnpm test scripts from other commands. Runner matching should parse supported launcher chains plus cwd, and reject ambiguous commands before execution.

suggestions.title: Resolve the guard bypass and verdict-command mismatch
suggestions.rationale: The MCP path checks profile.allowed_commands before the guard, but pnpm and cargo are not in the default allow-list. The native guard fails open for command substitution, redirection, and other unsupported compounds, and _run_guarded_invocations currently returns merged stdout/stderr. Also, select_tests.py has no executable shebang, so rewriting directly to scripts/sdd/select_tests.py is not a valid argv. Define an explicit supported-command boundary, invoke the CLI through python or a wrapper, and return only parsed verdict data from rewritten commands.

suggestions.title: Make cache and baseline behavior explicitly runner-scoped
suggestions.rationale: green_cache._is_cacheable accepts only .py files and its manifest hashes Python imports, pyproject files, and marker expressions. baseline.py always creates a Python checkout and reruns pytest through distribution_of. Once targets carry runner identity, generic cache filtering must not receive vitest, cargo, or E2E targets; otherwise it can drop them, attempt Python baseline classification, or record false green evidence.

suggestions.title: Centralize runner validation in the kernel checker
suggestions.rationale: check_task_graph.py duplicates pytest operand parsing and currently reports every non-pytest command as invisible to select_tests, while cache_test_contract.py delegates only the old contract parser. Schema 2 would otherwise have two sources of truth for runner recognition, broadness, and operand validation. Make the checker consume the registry and contract loader, including schema-1 lifting, and add failures for unknown runner, invalid cwd/crate/plan, and unsupported task-tier use.

suggestions.title: Inject a capability into the dispatcher instead of importing the engine
suggestions.rationale: LLMCodeDispatcher currently has no engine context, its tool schema is static, and _run_tool only dispatches local filesystem/command methods. The existing coder_run_validation API already enforces execution ownership, task declaration, idempotency, and supervisor admission. Add a per-dispatch validation capability or context object that exposes only the active task's subset and delegates to that API; absent capability must be a hard tool error.

suggestions.title: Add an explicit validation-retry state machine
suggestions.rationale: TaskOutcome has no validation_failed state, and _run_task treats a consolidation result as terminal. A second _run_attempt also creates a new worktree from the feature branch, so it cannot naturally repair the committed failing attempt. Persist the verdict on TaskResult/attempt telemetry, seed the same-seat repair worktree from the failed branch, count it as an attempt, emit one outcome per attempt, and keep validation reds separate from model-suspension failures.

suggestions.title: Separate per-runner deadlines from the plan deadline
suggestions.rationale: ValidationSupervisor currently applies one timeout deadline across the first invocation and all chained invocations. The proposed defaults differ substantially by runner, so a slow cargo suite can consume the entire budget before vitest runs and produce an ambiguous partial result. Track per-invocation timeout and an overall cap, mark only unfinished runners timed_out, preserve completed evidence, and fail closed without populating the green cache.

suggestions.title: Add runner-specific evidence fixtures before changing the parser spine
suggestions.rationale: parse_junit currently derives node ids only when testcase.file ends in .py and does not retain failure text, so it cannot directly produce bounded vitest excerpts. The current tests cover pytest xunit1 counts, unmapped cases, malformed XML, and missing files only. Add fixtures for TypeScript JUnit, nested suites, missing file attributes, cargo libtest output, E2E JSON, missing reports, nonzero exits, and excerpt truncation; assert any unmapped or unavailable failure remains red.

suggestions.title: Enforce runner tier eligibility at admission
suggestions.rationale: The kernel currently validates only the three global tiers and builds every plan through pytest-specific selection. The design says parrot-e2e is never task-tier, but without an adapter-level tier check a declared E2E runner can be silently omitted or accidentally executed by task validation. Reject an ineligible runner during contract/index validation with an explicit diagnostic; do not convert it into an empty green plan.

suggestions.title: Constrain TOML adapter loading to the stdlib kernel contract
suggestions.rationale: test_scope is imported as a top-level module under isolated system Python and is explicitly tested to avoid Pydantic and parrot imports. A dotted adapter path from repository TOML can violate that boundary or fail only in the native hook environment. Validate adapter interface, importability, runner kind, and tier/report capabilities during admission; fail closed with the config path and error rather than silently falling back to pytest.
